Explain why the value of x² + 1 can never be negative.
items.answer: x² is never negative (a square of a positive or negative number is positive or zero), so x² + 1 is at least 1.

items.stem: A formula is A = ½bh. Explain what happens to A when b is doubled and h stays the same.
items.answer: A doubles, because A is b multiplied by a fixed number (½h).

items.answer: (a) A fixed charge of $20 paid however far you drive. (b) 200 km

items.stem: Hana says that when y = 2, the value of 5y² is 100. Explain the mistake and give the correct value.
items.answer: Only y is squared: 5 × 2² = 5 × 4 = 20. Hana has worked out (5y)².
items.markingKey: B1 identifies the error; B1 correct value. [2]

items.stem: Explain why 3x² and (3x)² have different values when x = 2.
items.answer: 3x² = 3 × 4 = 12 (only x is squared) but (3x)² = 6² = 36 (the whole of 3x is squared).
items.markingKey: B1 each value with the order of operations explained. [2]

items.stem: Grace says the mean of the three numbers x, x + 7 and x + 14 is x + 7/3. Explain the mistake and give the correct mean.
items.answer: The whole total must be divided by 3: (3x + 21) ÷ 3 = x + 7.

items.stem: Explain the difference between an expression and a formula. Give an example of each.
items.answer: An expression has no equals sign, e.g. 3x + 2. A formula shows how one variable is calculated from others, e.g. A = lw.

items.stem: A shop sells pens at p cents each. Explain why the cost in dollars of 12 pens is 0.12p, not 12p.
items.answer: 12 pens cost 12p cents; there are 100 cents in a dollar, so 12p ÷ 100 = 0.12p dollars.
